name: Protopasta (Protoplant, Inc.)
summary: Protoplant, Inc. (dba "Protoplant, makers of Protopasta") is a US specialty filament maker founded in 2013 via Kickstarter by Dustin Cram, Aaron Cram and Alexander Dick. It extrudes all of its own product in Vancouver, Washington and is best known as an early pioneer of composite and filled PLA rather than a broad engineering-material catalog.

product_lines.name: HTPLA (High Temp PLA)
product_lines.notes: Annealable high-heat PLA: standard NatureWorks-type PLA resin plus a nucleating/crystallisation-promoter package, not a different base polymer. Covers all pigment/glitter/metallic/translucent colourways (Nebula Multicolor, Stardust Silver Glitter, Empire Strikes Black, Galactic Empire, Candy Apple, Cloverleaf, Mermaid's Tale, Iridescent Ice, Black Opaque). No dedicated high-heat-PLA id exists in this catalog.

product_lines.name: Matte Fiber HTPLA
product_lines.notes: HTPLA base with fibre filler: Walnut/Mahogany/Daffodil-type colourways are wood-flour filled (pla-wood); plain Matte Black/White/Gray use a matting additive (pla-matte).

product_lines.name: Carbon Fiber Composite PLA / HTPLA (incl. Recycled Carbon Fiber PLA)
product_lines.notes: PLA (NatureWorks 4043D family) + chopped/milled carbon fibre; Black, Light/Medium/Dark Gray colourways plus a recycled-content grade.

product_lines.name: Carbon Fiber PETG / Recycled Carbon Fiber PETG
product_lines.notes: PETG copolyester + carbon fibre; recycled-content variant is the same chemistry.

product_lines.name: Carbon Fiber PCTG (Black High-Strength / Gray High-Impact)
product_lines.notes: PCTG + carbon fibre. Listed against pctg for family context only — no pctg-cf id exists in this catalog, so this is not a clean chemistry match.

product_lines.name: Metal Composite PLA / HTPLA (Iron, Stainless Steel, Copper, Brass, Bronze)
product_lines.notes: PLA/HTPLA + powdered metal. Iron 1.8 g/cm3 (rustable, magnetic), stainless steel 2.4 g/cm3; High-Density grades are heavier still. Aesthetic/weight filler and polishable — not stronger than plain PLA and (steel grades) not electrically conductive.

product_lines.name: Electrically Conductive Composite PLA
product_lines.notes: NatureWorks 4043D PLA + dispersant + conductive carbon black; density 1.15 g/cm3, volume resistivity ~15 ohm-cm moulded and ~30-115 ohm-cm printed (XY vs Z). True conductive range, well below ESD; no conductive-PLA id exists.

product_lines.name: Static Dissipative PETG
product_lines.notes: PETG + conductive carbon black tuned into the 10^5-10^9 ohm ESD-safe band rather than the conductive range.

product_lines.name: Static Dissipative PLA / Static Dissipative Carbon Fiber PLA
product_lines.notes: PLA (and PLA-CF) base tuned into the 10^5-10^9 ohm ESD band. No PLA-ESD id exists; petg-esd is PETG-specific.

product_lines.name: Recycled PLA / Recycled PETG
product_lines.notes: Black Recycled PLA, Black Recycled PETG and Still Colorful Recycled PLA (018/033) — post-industrial/post-consumer regrind, no chemistry deviation from the virgin equivalents.

product_lines.name: Polyketone composites (Glass Fiber Polyketone / Carbon Fiber Polyketone)
product_lines.notes: Base polymer is aliphatic polyketone (PK), an engineering resin marketed as nylon-like; glass- or carbon-fibre reinforced. No polyketone id exists in this catalog.

product_lines.name: Flexible TPU / Rigid TPU
product_lines.notes: Clear Flexible TPU and Recycled Black Flexible TPU; Clear Rigid TPU is a higher-durometer grade of the same chemistry. Shore hardness not published, so no durometer-specific id is assigned.

product_lines.name: Flexible TPE (Black)
product_lines.notes: Non-urethane thermoplastic elastomer, softer/more rubbery than the TPU line per Protopasta's own copy.

additional_notes: Sold direct and through resellers (MatterHackers, 3DJake, Amazon, eBay), but production stays at Protoplant — no white-label manufacturing for other brands was found in either direction, so oem_relationships is empty rather than unknown. "All Protopasta products are produced at Protoplant, in Vancouver, Washington, USA"; no country-of-origin controversy surfaced. Runs a "CM Designs" collaboration line and a Filament Workshop education product, neither verified as a separate brand. Filament Cheat Sheet rates the brand Tier A-; exotic composites are commonly cited around $40-60+/kg but exact pricing is unverified.

provenance.conflicts: None. Price-tier placement rests on a third-party review-site rating plus unverified street-price ranges rather than a published price list.
